The raid party, minus the Japanese siblings on spawn killing duty, made their way to the second tower as quickly as the gloom shrouded cathedral grounds permitted.

"Why is there a hedge maze?" Luis asked, eyeing the feature as they jogged around it. "It doesn't really fit the feel of this place."

"This wasn't made by anyone." Aylin reminded him. The mage sounded a little winded, and Jade suspected she wasn't used to this much running around. "It's a random creation generated by the Labyrinth, using bits and pieces from your world."

She didn't answer any of Luis's follow up questions, wisely opting to conserve her energy. Jade, on the other hand, wasn't even breathing hard. She loped along at the head of the group with Tara, the two of them outpacing everyone other than Parker. They held back a little, making sure the group didn't get separated. They weren't likely to run into monsters yet, but it was better to be safe.

"Hey, Tara." Jade said, following the tek'kalla along a winding path through a dense cluster of trees. "Can I ask you something?"

"Sure. What is it?"

"I've been wondering for a while. You always talk about how spellcraft and mages are better than technology. So, why do you use that combat suit instead of enchanted robes like Aylin wears?"

"It's not that I hate magitech." The mage started slowly, considering the question. "Rather, I disagree with the stance that magitech stands superior to spellcraft in every way, or even a majority of ways. A stance that most of tek'kalla society is rapidly adopting. As an adjunct to traditional magic, it certainly has its place. As a wholesale replacement?" She sniffed in derision. "Well, I haven't heard any complaints from you."

"And you won't. I'm glad we have someone who understands magic theory on the team. You won't get that from me, Luis, or Naomi."

"And that's the other thing. My people are slowly losing their grasp on the fundamentals of arcane knowledge that led us to success. These days, only magitech engineers have more than a basic grasp on magical theory. In my grandfather's generation, no one dared take on a Wayfarer trial without one or more team members with a solid grounding in it."

"I'm hoping I'll have the chance to learn more myself. Hopefully things stop trying to kill us for long enough for me to get started.""I wouldn't bet on that being anytime soon." Tara said, a slight grin pulling at the corners of her lips. "In the short time I've known you, it's been one crisis after another. If anything, empirical evidence suggests further escalation in the near future."

"You're probably right." Jade muttered. "Still, a girl can dream."

When they drew close to the second tower, Jade called a halt. After a quick check-in with Aki to make sure she and her brother were still okay, she gathered everybody together to go over a revised plan. This time, Jade would scale the tower and destroy the barrier sphere alone while everyone else remained at a safe distance. If everything proceeded the same way it had at the first tower, she would fly down to rejoin the team as they engaged the newly spawned monsters. If the Labyrinth had something else in store for them, well, Jade was best suited for escaping any unexpected danger.

"This time, we'll fight them as a team." Jade finished, glancing at Tara for confirmation. The mage nodded.

"I have the mana for another fireball of that size, but even with the enhanced regeneration rate we're experiencing, I don't want to use it. Besides." she gave her right arm a tender rub. "My mana circuits are still recovering from the first Core. I shouldn't strain them further."

"That's alright." Luis grinned at her. "You have to give the rest of us a chance to show off, too."

"Leave big ones to me." Urgraan croaked, slamming a fist into a webbed palm with a wet slapping sound. "I knock them down. You keep them down."

"Good plan." Parker said, drawing his blades. "Simple, and to the point."

"Then let's get to it."

Jade lifted off the ground with a powerful flap of her wings. For a few moments she allowed herself to revel once again in the boundless joy of flight before forcing herself to focus and land atop the tower. An identical mechanical contraption rose from the roof, complete with a glowing glass sphere. Just as before, it emanated a ray of brilliant energy that stretched over the cathedral grounds before disappearing through a high window. Not letting her guard down, Jade carefully inspected the area before proceeding to the device. Not finding any signs of danger, she signaled to her friends below and then summoned her aura blades. A single, powerful slash was enough to splinter the sphere and cleave the odd device holding it in two, releasing another blast of heat as it collapsed. The second beam of light faded away a moment later, leaving only two remaining.

Jade was already back in the sky before the tower roof began to crack, arcing back to her friends on the ground even as the shrieks of more monsters clawing their way from the ground rose to meet her. They were in luck. The pattern from the first tower held, and there weren't any unpleasant surprises. Spotting an especially tight cluster of Corrupted Spirits, Jade fired off a Clinging Darkness before reaching the ground. The spell had finally broken through the C-rank threshold, and its subsequent improvement was dramatic.

Spell: Clinging Darkness

Rating: C level spell

Cost: Low mana

Duration: 10 seconds

Cooldown: 30 seconds

Effect: Shroud a nearby area in a sphere of darkness. Any creature that enters the sphere is afflicted with blindness for the duration. The ability to see in the dark does not allow creatures to perceive anything inside the effect of this spell, although you can see through the darkness created by it.

The sphere of darkness wasn't especially large, but it was big enough to catch three enemies within its radius. Jade managed to take two of them down before they broke free of the earth, and chased after the third as it stumbled clear of her spell. The blindness affliction persisted even after the monster broke out of the sphere, thick shadows continuing to swirl around its face. She easily dodged its wild slashes, finishing it off with a double slash across its chest.

That's a handy upgrade. Jade thought with a slight grin, dismissing the cloud of gloom. Time to put it to use.

The battle wasn't quite as easy as the first, but that was expected. Without Tara blowing up a solid third of the monsters before they reached the raid group, and having two fewer combatants, the speed and strength of the higher-level creatures proved a decent challenge. It was nothing their team couldn't handle, however, and they fell into the strategies formed during their week of training. Naomi and Siora stayed in the rear providing healing and buffs while Aylin focused on projecting magical shields. Tara remained with them, both as a backline guard and as a source of ranged damage. Luis and Urgraan stayed together at the front, trading blows with the heavily armored templars and keeping them busy long enough for Parker and Fenrin to wear them down.

Jade didn't form up with the rest of the party. She remained in the periphery of the engagement, striking like a phantom. One moment she was dropping rune traps to ensnare the monsters, leaving them an easy target for Tara and Fenrin. The next she was finishing off a wounded templar with a strike to the neck and charming its companion, commanding it to turn on its fellows. She utilized her advanced class spell, enrapture, to effectively stun any collection of monsters that got too clumped up, leaving them out of the fight for critical periods. Her companions knew not to damage any of the stupefied monsters, allowing them to wait out the duration of the debuff while they teamed up on the rest. Just before the spell broke Jade would swoop back into their midst, leveraging her Heartbreaker ability to critically strike vital points and take down as many as she could before vanishing to harass a different group.

The fight finally came to a close with Luis, empowered with buffs cast by Naomi and Siora, clashing with the final Templar. The armored monster swung down with a blade wreathed in purple flames only for it to meet Luis's shield with a flash of silver light. His 'Reflect' talent was the newest addition to his suite of abilities, and while it was more effective at redirecting magical damage than physical, it proved to be quite capable of redirecting less esoteric forces. The Templar fell lifelessly to the ground, its battered and dented armor scorched by its own fell flames.

"Everyone okay?" Jade asked, one hand held against her earpiece as she jogged to join Luis. "Check in."

She couldn't see any more monsters in the area, but that didn't mean there weren't any. The corespace's increased magic was interfering with magical senses, making it harder than usual to detect nearby creatures. Though they tried to stay in a loose group, the currents of battle had left them scattered throughout the lightly wooded region of the cathedral's grounds. One by one, everyone reported their areas as clear. There were a few lingering injuries for Siora and Naomi to tend to, but other than that, the fight had gone well.

"There are still a few coming up from the ground here." Parker's voice came over Jade's earpiece. "Looks like it's the same as the first tower."

"We planned for this." Jade responded. "Urgraan, Ellie, will the two of you be able to handle the stragglers?"

"Already stomped one." the rhyssit croaked.

"I'm with him. We will take care of them." Ellie added.

"Great, just be careful and let us know if anything changes." Jade took a calming breath. Her heart was still pounding from the combined exertion and thrill of battle. She needed to stay focused on the bigger picture. This was a bigger operation than most of them were used to. "Aki, Eita? Everything still okay back there?"

"If anything, they're slowing down here." Aki answered calmly.

"You sure you don't need help?" Her brother cut in. "I'm ready to join the fun anytime.""This isn't a game, Eita." Jade admonished. "Keep your head in the-"

She cut herself off before accidentally undermining her statement with an unfortunate turn of phrase.

"What was that?""Just, stay focused. When the last tower falls, we'll need all hands on deck for the boss fight.""We'll be ready." Aki promised.

A few minutes later, the remaining group members who weren't keeping the grounds clear behind them gathered and headed towards the third tower. Jade did a quick head count and grimaced. They couldn't afford to leave the completed zones empty to continually spawn more monsters, but leaving two people behind after each one was a substantial hit to their combat power. The remaining group was Jade's full team, including Siora, plus Parker and Aylin. She moved next to Tara, who was again leading the group.

"Assuming the next two towers are similar, we shouldn't have a problem with this one. If we take on the fourth with six people, though, things could go wrong fast."

Despite their inflated levels, the monsters weren't very hardy. They quickly fell to coordinated teamwork. The real problem was damage. When they did land an attack, they hit hard.

"We could pull the whole team back together at the last moment and take the final swarm with a big group." Tara suggested. "If we're quick, it won't leave much time for monsters to spawn elsewhere.""Maybe... but this boss is going to be especially powerful. If we keep the zones clear right up until we start the fight, we could get more time to focus fire on it. Can you manage another fireball?"

Tara didn't answer immediately. Jade could see her eyes scanning her displays through the translucent visor, and the tek'kalla rubbed at her right forearm.

"Yes, I can." She said finally. Her expression didn't give anything away, but Jade could sense a hint of uncertainty in her emotions.

"Are you sure? If you hurt yourself before we get to the boss-"

"I can do it." She repeated more firmly, drawing a few glances from the others. "But if I use that much power again so soon, I won't have it ready for the boss."

"That's alright, huge explosions aren't the best way to take on one enemy."

Tara folded her arms and gave Jade a look.

"Okay, huge explosions would probably be helpful there too." She conceded. "But we'll make do. We have a lot of damage in this group."

Parker, Ellie, Eita, and Urgraan were all on Luis's level or better when it came strictly to dealing damage and racking up kills. It made for some powerful blitzing opportunities, a tactic Jade hoped to employ against the boss. They needed to end this as soon as possible, and there was no better way than via overwhelming firepower.

Is Tara infecting me? Jade mused, reflecting on the thought. But no, she'd always preferred the direct approach. Tara was simply a kindred spirit.

The battle at the third tower played out in much the same way as the first two, but with two key differences. Their reduced numbers, which they'd anticipated, and the different enemies, which they had not. Instead of more Templars and Corrupted Spirits, the now-reduced party was met with a rush of radiant monsters. Most of the enemies were Celestial Spirits, the same knight-like creatures that emerged from the portal when Jade first opened it. This time they were accompanied by Sanctified Spirits, a creature that took the form of a long, brown robe filled with dazzling radiance. The light was so bright that it took Jade physically stabbing one of them with Phantom for her to realize that there actually was a body wearing the cloak, and that the monster wasn't incorporeal.

It was a bad match up for Jade. The swords wielded by the Celestial Spirits were shrouded in incandescent energy, and the Sanctified Spirits were even worse. They conjured beams of radiant energy, standing back and flinging them into the party's flanks as they battled the rest of the wave. Again, Jade took on the role of disrupter. Leaving her teammates to support each other, she wove in and out of the enemy's back line and made full use of her invisibility spell to keep the enemy off balance with unexpected strikes. That did a lot to ease the pressure on the rest of the team, but not everything worked as well as she hoped. Much to Jade's frustration, the Sanctified Spirits proved quite resilient against her charm effects. This blunted her effectiveness and prevented her from striking any definitive blows, but that was alright. Her goal wasn't to tear through the priestly spirits; it was to keep them occupied.

By the time Luis and Parker took down the last of the knights and moved to join her, she wasn't in the best shape. Jade was easily the most evasive member of the raid party, but even she couldn't weave through a dozen high level enemies relentlessly targeting her with heavenly fire and emerge unscathed. She backed off while the damage dealers moved in to clean up the Sanctified Spirits, warning Siora before dropping her invisibility beside the elf.

"Jade! You're covered in burns!" Siora gasped, raising her right hand as it began to glow with a soft, warm light. "Let me-""No." Jade pushed her hand down, nodding towards the battle. "Focus on the people in danger."

"But-"

"I'll make it another few minutes, I'm safe now."

"Next time, tell me when you're in trouble." Siora sighed, redirecting the healing spell to Fenrin.

Jade didn't respond. She gritted her teeth against the stinging pain of what felt like a dozen sunburns seared into her flesh. The demonic vulnerability to incandescent energy wasn't to be taken lightly.

I need to be careful with the boss.

If regular monsters dealt this much damage to her through her Seducer's Mantle defensive bonuses, then the boss would be even more dangerous.

The fight ended without incident. The weight of fatigue was beginning to settle on Jade's shoulders, lingering even after Siora and Naomi healed her wounds. But there was no time to rest. Just as the group finished healing, the first of the post-wave monsters began to spawn. Unlike on the other half of the cathedral grounds, the Celestial creatures didn't claw their way up through the dirt. Instead, they manifested in a pillar of light that descended from the sky, slowly taking shape over the course of about a minute. Fortunately, they shared the vulnerability the other monsters in this space possessed: taking increased damage while in the process of spawning.

"Parker, Aylin, you two handle this." Jade said, helping the veteran cut one of the Sanctified Spirits to ribbons before it could gain substance. "We'll be quick. Tara is going all out on this one.""Good." He grunted, stepping back from the dead monster and scanning the area for the next. "We're starting to flag, and we haven't even reached the real fight yet."

"Agreed." Jade did a quick survey of the group. She knew her party members well enough to see that they were wearing down fast. But their training had pushed them harder than this. "We can do it. One more big push."

"We'll be ready."

"Jade!" Aylin waved her over before she could get the party moving. "Wait for a moment!"

"What is it?" She asked, jogging over.

"Look, here." Aylin pulled a crystal rod out of a pouch and held it up, showing her a sequence of blinking lights. Jade just blinked, slowly looking between it and her.

"…What am I looking at?"

"That's a field resonance detector." Tara explained, stepping around Jade to peer at it. Her eyes widened. "…it's increasing?" The tek'kalla asked Aylin.

"It is.""What is increasing?" Jade asked, a little annoyed. "We're short on time, here.""Even shorter than we thought." Aylin said grimly. "The magical saturation of this space is increasing at an increasing rate. It started after we destroyed the first tower."

"And if we can measure that change in the half hour we've been fighting, that's very bad." Tara added. "My guess, and it's only a guess, is that the Core is growing more unstable as it generates more monsters."

"More unstable?" Jade asked, confused. "I thought it raised the level of the monsters it was creating to fix that."

"A process that strains it more the longer it goes on. We can't know for sure, but I doubt this place is capable of going back even to the state we found it in without us getting to the Core and finding a way to safely disperse the overload ourselves. Basically." Aylin took a deep breath. "We do this in one try, or we don't do it at all."

When training together for the raid Aylin had explained to the group that if things went sideways in the corespace, retreating outside and waiting to try again was a valid approach. The Labyrinth would reset corespaces after a certain amount of time, and there was no limit to the number of attempts a team could make at reaching the Core. But all that was before they knew that this one was well on its way to the magical equivalent of a nuclear meltdown.

"If we leave and this place goes boom, what will the damage be to our home?" Luis asked.

"I have no idea. This is far beyond the scope of my studies." Aylin just shook her head. "The consequences could be anything from minimal to catastrophic."

"We're here and we're close." Jade said, mindful that the situation was only getting worse while they talked. "We make one big push. If the boss is too dangerous, we'll retreat, but we have to try."The team all nodded. One way or another, the Core wasn't long for this world. If they couldn't beat the boss, they would have to leave and hope the damage wasn't too bad when it finally blew.

"Great talk, now let's get moving." Tara said, already jogging towards the fourth and final tower. "I'm ready to blow something up."
